# rust-camel

> rust-camel is Apache Camel rewritten in Rust: the same routes, Enterprise Integration Patterns, endpoint URIs, Simple expressions and YAML DSL, as a single native binary with no third-party dependencies. It starts in about 10 ms, uses about 10 MB of memory and is 2.5-8x faster than Apache Camel 4.23 on Java 21 in the published benchmarks. It is aimed at AI agents (as their integration and action layer), serverless and edge deployments. It is an independent project, not affiliated with the Apache Software Foundation.

Key facts:

- Language: Rust, standard library only (TLS, HTTP/2, gRPC, AMQP, MQTT, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB, Cassandra protocols written from scratch).
- About 230 components, languages and data formats; all Camel EIPs; Rust, YAML and XML DSLs; REST DSL; Kamelets; a Camel-JBang-style `camel` CLI.
- AI integrations: OpenAI-compatible chat and embeddings, AWS Bedrock (Converse, streaming, guardrails, Agent Runtime), Azure OpenAI (tool calls, Assistants), Google Vertex AI (Gemini, partner models).
- Not yet packaged: MCP server, native AWS Lambda runtime, vector store components (build-it-yourself patterns are documented).
- License: Apache-2.0.

- [Features](https://github.com/pmsudhi/Rust-camel/blob/main/docs/FEATURES.md): every component, language and data format with its options
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/pmsudhi/Rust-camel/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md): planned work and patterns for agents and serverless
- [Architecture](https://github.com/pmsudhi/Rust-camel/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): internals and conventions
- [Interop](https://github.com/pmsudhi/Rust-camel/blob/main/docs/INTEROP.md): verification against real servers, official clients and emulators
